summary: Weekly POC check-in for Nimbus Analytics pilot. Focused on onboarding progress, access setup (VPC/IAM), and environment readiness for benchmark runs. Discussed initial tuning levers (batching, quantization, prefix caching), agreed to run three benchmark scenarios, and clarified security artifacts to share. Next steps: share docs/diagrams, provide test account info, schedule benchmark, and reconvene after initial results.
topics: VPC peering and IAM role details
Benchmark plan: hosted vs dedicated vs quantized
Security & compliance artifacts (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
transcript:
[00:00] Emma (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. Quick roll call? I see Carlos, Priya, Liam — can you hear us okay?
[00:08] Carlos (Nimbus): Yep, loud and clear.
[00:10] Liam (Nimbus): Here.
[00:12] Priya (Nimbus): Good afternoon.
[00:15] Samir (Redwood SE): Hi all, Samir here from Redwood, glad to sync.
[00:18] Emma: Cool. Agenda for today: onboarding checklist, what we still need for access, the benchmark runs we talked about, and any blockers. We'll aim to capture action items.
[00:28] Carlos: Sounds good. Quick update from our side: we've created the test AWS account and flagged the security team — Priya will share the details after this call. We're still waiting on the VPC CIDR from networking, but should have that by tomorrow.
[00:40] Priya: Yes, correct. I can share VPC CIDR and IAM role ARNs — little note, our networking team runs strict egress rules so we might need to allow some Redwood IP ranges.
[00:50] Emma: We can give you our dedicated peering ranges — I'll include that in the template. Note that for the hosted benchmark step, peering is optional; we can run an initial test over the public API with sample data to validate latency and cost profile.
[01:05] Liam: For stake, what are we measuring in the benchmark? P50/P95 latency and cost per 1k requests?
[01:12] Samir: Yes, standard: P50, P95, tokens/sec throughput, and estimated $/1k tokens. We'll run three scenarios: 1) Redwood hosted (no VPC) baseline, 2) Redwood Dedicated on a small reserved pool to measure predictability, 3) quantized model variant to measure cost reduction and impact on quality.
[01:30] Carlos: On quality, we need to check regression against our golden prompts — we have a suite of 120 prompts. Will Redwood run evals against those automatically or do we push them?
[01:42] Samir: We can ingest your prompt set — preferred if you push them to the S3 test bucket we provide or paste into the drive link. We'll run automated evals and provide diffs. Heads up: quantized variants sometimes have minor tokenization differences — we'll call those out.
[01:58] Emma: Also, regarding caching — if you use a prefix-heavy workload, our KV cache can reduce token cost significantly, but it's something we enable on the deployment config. We'll note that as an experimental toggle during benchmark.
[02:12] Priya: For private deployments, we were also exploring Redwood Private, potentially on-prem. Does that require any additional security review?
[02:20] Emma: Yes, for Private deployments there's a separate package — we'll bring in the security team and a separate SOW. But for the POC pilot, we recommend starting with hosted or Dedicated to get baseline numbers quickly, then discuss Private if required by compliance.
[02:35] Carlos: Ok. On compliance, can you confirm SOC2 and KMS support? Our legal needs to see key management and audit logs.
[02:43] Emma: We are SOC 2 Type II — I'll share the report and a security pack. We support BYOK via KMS for Dedicated/Private. Audit logs and token-level tracing are available in the Console. I'll attach the redwood-sec.pdf.
[02:58] Liam: Great. A small thing: when you say "Dedicated", is that a reserved GPU pool we provision?
[03:06] Samir: Dedicated is reserved capacity. For pilots we often spin up a small pool — e.g., 2-4 GPUs depending on model size. For POC we can use a transient small pool with a short commitment; sales will follow with pricing, but the point is to show predictable latency.
[03:22] Carlos: Budget is a constraint. We'll need the estimate for the three scenarios. Maybe an order of magnitude first.
[03:28] Emma: Absolutely — I'll send a short spreadsheet estimating cost per scenario based on token volumes you gave us earlier.
[03:34] Priya: Back to access — do you need us to open ports, or just provide peering and an IAM role?
[03:41] Samir: For VPC peering we just need the VPC CIDR and a cross-account role to allow the provisioning of endpoints. If peering isn't possible, we can do a private link or run via public API and lock down via IP allowlists. We'll send both templates.
[03:56] Carlos: How long until you can run the hosted baseline if we share the prompt set now?
[04:01] Samir: If you give us the prompts and a small trace of traffic (sample requests), we can run a hosted baseline within 24–48 hours. Dedicated and quantized runs will take a bit longer due to provisioning and model conversion — estimate 3–5 business days.
[04:15] Liam: OK. A couple of technical clarifications: 1) Does Redwood support KV cache across requests for multi-turn contexts? 2) How do you handle session affinity for caching?
[04:26] Samir: Yes, KV cache support is in the runtime. For multi-turn, the cache keeps prefix tokens in memory and reuses KV for compatible requests. We support session keys — we can persist small caches or drop them depending on memory constraints. Affinity is handled by routing policy; for Dedicated we can pin sessions to instances to maximize cache hits.
[04:42] Priya: Any particular model formats we need to provide? Our team uses a custom finetuned model but it's exportable as an HF checkpoint.
[04:49] Samir: HF checkpoints are fine. For Dedicated/Private we do an onboarding step to validate model architecture and run a quick dry-run. For quantization we'll convert to a quantized variant; we'll note any accuracy regressions.
[05:00] Carlos: We also want to test rate limiting behavior — what happens if we burst above provisioned capacity?
[05:06] Emma: We have graceful throttling and fallback policies — requests can fall back to a lower-cost model variant or queue; for SLA-critical paths we recommend a small buffer in Dedicated capacity and can configure autoscale triggers. We'll include recommended autoscale settings in the checklist.
[05:22] Liam: Thanks. On the golden prompts, are you able to return full tokens or do you strip system prompts? We need raw outputs for diffing.
[05:30] Samir: We can return raw outputs and full token logs if you opt in — that's available in the Console under traces. We'll include instructions on enabling token logs (note: token logs increase storage retention costs).
[05:42] Priya: One question about encryption—if we use KMS, is the customer key visible to Redwood ops?
[05:48] Emma: With BYOK and KMS policies, you retain control of the key; only the encrypted data is visible to Redwood. For Private/on-prem we can do zero-knowledge setups. We'll put the security team on the follow-up thread to clarify details.
[06:02] Carlos: This is all good. Let's confirm the timeline: Priya will share account and VPC info by 12/04, Emma will send security pack and onboarding checklist by 12/03, Samir will run the hosted baseline within 48 hours of receiving prompts and then schedule Dedicated/quantized runs by 12/08.
[06:20] Emma: Correct. Any blockers we haven't covered?
[06:24] Liam: Not from Product. We just want clear pass/fail on the golden prompts so we can sign off for the pilot.
[06:31] Samir: We'll produce a simple regression report, with pass/fail thresholds you define — default is 95% exact-match on intent-class or 90% BLEU-ish metric, but we can accept your criteria.
[06:43] Carlos: We'll confirm success criteria by 12/06.
[06:47] Emma: Perfect. Last thing — I'll drop links in the meeting notes: onboarding checklist, VPC template, SOC2, and a short pricing spreadsheet. Also Samir will attach the benchmark plan with exact commands and flags we use.
[07:00] Priya: Thanks — that's helpful.
[07:02] Emma: Okay great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in the thread.
[07:07] Carlos: Thanks all.
[07:08] Liam: Bye.
[07:09] Priya: Bye.
